sections.h2: Where is Melbourne in Brevard County?
sections.html:
Melbourne is in southern Brevard County, southeast of Orlando on the east coast, and it straddles the Indian River Lagoon. Most of the city lies on the mainland, while a smaller piece sits on a barrier island across the water.

That split gives sellers two very different kinds of property under one city name. The city measures 51.59 square miles, or 33,016.28 acres, as of March 2026, and the Bureau of Economic and Business Research put its 2025 population at 88,499.

The city calls itself the economic engine of Brevard County, pointing to high-tech employers, its Space Coast location and ties with regional schools and research groups. A council appoints a city manager under the charter, and the council also sets the budget and the city's tax rate after public hearings.

  • Ask your insurer for the premium history, since a buyer will price it in.
  • Confirm the parcel is inside city limits before you quote city rules to a buyer.
  • Find the permit history before you list.

sections.h2: Does Melbourne's permit system affect a quick sale?
sections.html:
Yes, because a buyer's inspector or lender will ask whether past work was permitted. The city's building section says permits are needed for many jobs people overlook: carports, garages, fences, sheds, re-roofing, window and door replacement, A/C change-outs, electrical, plumbing, gas piping and generators.

Starting work without a permit can bring a penalty of 100 percent of the usual permit fee, and the city warns that structures built without one may end up removed. Structures also have to respect setbacks and stay out of easements, and a variance request goes through the Community Development Department.

A residential permit typically takes 5 to 7 working days for approval or a response on a single review. If you are fixing something to satisfy a buyer, count that time in. Owner-builder permits are only available when the property is not for sale or lease for a period of one year, so a house headed to market generally needs a licensed contractor for permitted repairs.

sections.h2: What paperwork does a Melbourne permit application need?
sections.html:
The city's online system asks for drawings where they apply, a survey for any new construction or addition, proof of ownership in the form of a deed or tax statement, a description of the work and an estimated construction value.

Permits expire on a clock. An application or issued permit goes inactive after 180 days without activity, with another 180 days to reinstate by uploading a letter that gives the permit number, address, reason for inactivity and an expected completion date.

An old unfinished permit is worth closing out. Ask the building section which permits are still open for your address.

sections.h2: How do Brevard property taxes line up with a Melbourne sale?
sections.html:
Brevard's property appraiser assesses the parcel, while the tax collector mails the bill. Florida runs one yearly schedule in every county.

  • January 1: the value is fixed for the year.
  • March 1: last day to file for exemptions.
  • August: the proposed tax notice arrives.
  • November: bills go out with a 4 percent early-pay discount.
  • April 1: unpaid bills turn delinquent.

Have the closing agent prorate the year's bill between both parties, and keep the receipt. Request the unpaid balance, if any, from the Brevard tax collector before agreeing to a closing date.

sections.h2: What happens to my homestead benefits if I sell?
sections.html:
They end on that parcel. The $50,000 exemption ceiling stops applying, and the cap that held your assessed value below market lapses for the next owner, whose bill is based on full just value after the following January 1.

You may be able to carry your cap to a new Florida home. The state says the new homestead must be set up within three years counted from the start of the year in which you left the old home, and the portability form is filed with the homestead application by March 1.

The Department of Revenue's cap chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025.

sections.h2: What do deed stamps and recording cost in Melbourne?
sections.html:
Brevard uses the standard Florida deed stamp, at the 70 cent rate per hundred dollars of price listed by the state's revenue department. The clerk collects the tax at recording, and each signer of the deed shares liability for it.

Recording is priced per page under section 28.24, and the clerk adds trust fund and technology charges. The state lists quit claim, warranty and life estate deeds as taxable, and a deed from an estate's court-appointed representative as not taxable.

sections.h2: What if the Melbourne house has a tenant, probate or a foreclosure?
sections.html:
Each situation changes the schedule, not the ability to sell. A tenant on a month-to-month lease needs a 30-day notice, and a nonpayment notice runs 3 days excluding weekends and court holidays.

An heir needs authority from the court before signing. Estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets, or a death more than two years back, can use summary administration. Florida levies no estate tax for deaths after December 31, 2004.

In a foreclosure, the court sale is set for a date 20 to 35 days past the final judgment unless the lender agrees to a later date.

sections.h2: What other Melbourne rules can trip up a seller?
sections.html:
The city's list of permitted work also covers driveways, parking lots, roofing, irrigation systems, tree removal, signs and land-disturbing activity. A seller who paved, trimmed or replaced anything major should look for the paperwork.

Plans must be signed and sealed when residential work attaches to the main structure, includes an in-ground pool or has to meet wind load rules, such as a flag pole, satellite dish, aluminum construction or solar panels. Keep copies for the buyer's side.

Contractors applying for permits must show state certification or registration, a Brevard County competency card where required, and proof of workers' compensation coverage or an exemption affidavit. If you hire help to close out a permit, check those credentials.

sections.h2: How should I weigh a Melbourne cash offer?
sections.html:
Put the written cash figure beside what a listing would leave you after commission, repairs and the months of carrying costs. Then read the contract for who pays the deed stamp, the title policy and recording.

Skip any buyer who asks for a fee up front. Get the settlement date and the closing agent's name in writing, and ask whether the buyer expects you to finish any open permits before closing. Compare two or three written offers if you can, because terms differ as much as price.

faqs.q: Is Melbourne, FL in Brevard County?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's own page places it in southern Brevard County on Florida's east coast, southeast of Orlando, on both sides of the Indian River Lagoon.
The city's page lists 88,499 residents, from the Bureau of Economic and Business Research for 2025.

faqs.q: Can I get an owner-builder permit if I plan to sell?
faqs.a: Generally no. The city's FAQ says the property must not be for sale or lease for a period of one year to qualify, so a listed house usually needs a contractor.

faqs.q: How long does a Melbourne residential permit take?
faqs.a: The building section says residential permits typically average 5 to 7 working days for approval or a response on a single review, and some issue within 3 days.

faqs.q: What deed stamp rate applies in Brevard County?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100, the figure the state revenue department gives for all counties but Miami-Dade.
